Step–1 : Identify the reagent A  

Cyclohexene (a 2-π component) gives 8,8-diiodobicyclo[4.2.0]octan-7-one.  
The product is a cyclobutanone fused to the original cyclohexane ring; such a four-membered ring is obtained by a [2+2] cyclo-addition of a ketene with an alkene.

           O                          O
        I2C=C=O   +   cyclohexene  →   gem-I2–cyclobutanone fused to the ring

Therefore A must be the diiodo-ketene 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one, not the already-formed cyclobutenone.

Step–2 : Order of diene reactivity (B)

Reactivity in the Diels–Alder reaction depends mainly on
 • availability of the s-cis conformation,
 • electron density of the diene.

Most reactive → least reactive:

3. Cyclopenta-1,3-diene  
   – locked in the s-cis form and highly electron-rich.

1. 2,3-Dimethyl-1,3-butadiene  
   – readily attains s-cis; two methyl groups donate by hyperconjugation.

2. (2E,4E)-Hexa-2,4-diene  
   – has to rotate to s-cis but suffers less steric clash than the Z,Z isomer.

4. (2Z,4Z)-Hexa-2,4-diene  
   – rotation to s-cis places the two methyl groups on the same side and is sterically hindered, making it the least reactive.

Hence the correct sequence is 3  > 1  > 2  > 4.

Step–3 : Match with the options

Only option (C) combines  
A = 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one and  
B = 3, 1, 2, 4.

Answer: C
